statement: Snapshot caches have ttl = null and throw on failed reads, whoever creates them (a snapshot cache built outside the starter is pinned all the same), and no customizer replaces a CoSec cache's codec, loaders, key filter or per-entry lifetime; an instance refuses to start when Redis's maxmemory-policy is not noeviction, or cannot be read: a read that times out, loses its connection or gets a transient reply is tried again within CoCache's own bounds (5 attempts, pauses from 500 ms doubling to 2 s), a refused INFO is not, and a policy still unread is never safe; the reason names what happened, a timeout as a timeout and a refusal as a permission.
guards: spring-boot:CoSecPipelineAutoConfigurationTest#Redis that may evict snapshots fails startup unless told to warn
spring-boot:CoSecPipelineAutoConfigurationTest#a maxmemory-policy that cannot be read fails startup unless told to warn
spring-boot:SnapshotEvictionHealthIndicatorTest#the checks read the snapshot runtime's backend, not another backend bean
spring-boot:EvictionPolicyReadTest#a read that times out is tried again, and the next answer decides - SNP-3
spring-boot:EvictionPolicyReadTest#five reads that time out are a timeout, never a safe policy, and fail startup - SNP-3
spring-boot:EvictionPolicyReadTest#a refused INFO is not tried again, and says it is a permission - SNP-3
spring-boot:EvictionPolicyReadTest#an evicting policy read on a retry still fails startup - SNP-3
spring-boot:EvictionPolicyReadTest#a failure no retry would change is not tried again, and is still not safe - SNP-3
spring-boot:EvictionPolicyReadTest#the periodic re-check reads once, with no pause, and names a timeout as a timeout - SNP-3
